question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom /Phrase.

To pick holes in someone's coat

options.text: To deceive someone for personal gain

solution:
The correct answer is "**To find fault with someone."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The idiom "to pick holes in someone's coat" means to criticize or find fault with someone.**(किसी की आलोचना करना या दोष निकालना)
 
• This phrase is often used to describe someone who is being overly critical or nitpicking.
 
• The word "pick" in this context means to choose or select, while "holes" refers to flaws or imperfections.
 
 
• Example: As soon as I presented my argument, he began to pick holes in it.
 
 
 
• Thus, it is clear that option 3 is the correct definition of the given idiom.

Hence,** the correct answer is option 3**.
